chapter: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris
title: Conrad Janis's Tailgate Jazz Band on Circle
summary: Back in New York he recorded for Rudi Blesh's Circle label in 1950-51, including Down By The Riverside vocal.

bands.name: Conrad Janis and His Tailgate Jazz Band

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: When you got back to New York, then, you started working with Conrad Janis. And that eventually led to some recordings of Conrad Janis and His Tailgate Jazz Band. This is in November of 1950. There's Dick Smith on cornet...,
Yes.
...Tom Sharpstein on clarinet...,
Yes.
...Bob Green on piano...,
Yes.
...Danny Barker, Pops Foster... Again, there's Pops Foster; you and Pops Foster working very close together.
Moore (III) - 61
Who's that guy that got that date together? Rudi Blesh?
Rudi Blesh, okay. This is for Circle.
Circle, right.
Circle Records, yeah. And you recorded a number of selections, did you... "Tiger Rag," a lot of the New Orleans favorites, and then some others in the New Orleans spirit...
"Down By The Riverside"?

Let's see. I don't think "Down By The Riverside" is listed here. But there's "Tiger Rag," there's "Yellow Dog Blues," "Bugle Boy March," "Kansas City Stomps," and there's a whole list of things -- "1919 March" is one of them. Then in May of 1951, Conrad Janis, Dick Smith, Tom Sharpstein, Danny Barker was playing guitar, apparently there was no bass player, but Elmer Shobel(?) was playing piano replacing Bob Green. Do you remember that date in New York?
Mmm-hmm. Yes.
For Circle Records. "Eh La-Bas," "Willie The Weeper," "When You And I Were Young," and yeah, "Down By The Riverside." You have a vocal on that.
Yes.
Moore (III) - 62
Okay. Now, you recorded and you got some vocals here. Were these the first vocals that you recorded? Was that about the first time that you recorded singing?
Was that before the Village Vanguard?
Well, this is, I think, after the Village Vanguard. This is 1951. After you were first there.
I think that was my first vocal after that, "Down By The Riverside."
